cases.name: bad-optionlike
cases.why: Added by the issue #970 re-examination. A file NAMED after a flag: without the '--' option terminator the linter reads it as --help, prints usage and exits 0 having examined nothing, and the gate reports a confident 0 findings. Nothing in the original pair depended on that terminator.

cases.name: good-fixture-skip
cases.why: Added by the issue #970 re-examination. A deliberately-broken script sitting at controls/*/cases/*, which the gate must SKIP - that population belongs to the control that owns it. Nothing in the original pair depended on the exclusion. The offender is extensionless on purpose: a *.sh name would also be caught by the vendored anchor, which globs *.sh, and an anchor disagreeing on a known-GOOD input cannot isolate the blindness under test.

cases.name: bad-note-severity
cases.why: Added by issue #972, which raised the gate's default severity from error to style after reviewing the sub-error residual to zero. The file's ONLY finding is SC2002, a style-level note. Every earlier BAD case offends at error severity, so none of them could tell the raised default from the old one: revert the default to error and the whole register stayed green. This case is what reddens. MEASURED both ways: the gate at error, and the vendored anchor, report it clean; the gate at style reports the finding.

cases.name: unknown-zero-matched
cases.why: Added by issue #1129, which gave the register a third registrable expectation. A root holding no shell file at all: the gate must REFUSE ('0 examined is not 0 findings', #952) rather than report a confident clean, and exits 2 with its UNKNOWN marker. This is the first case in the tree to exercise a gate's refusal half - the branch whose failure is hardest to notice from outside, because a blind clean and a real clean are the same bytes. It is anchorable because ed5349c refuses this input too (MEASURED); an anchor predating the refusal branch would report clean here and land INERT.

anchors.note: PERMANENTLY UNRESOLVABLE AFTER SQUASH, BY DESIGN. This is a pre-squash commit on the #960 branch; squash-merging orphans it, so `git show` can never resolve it on main. That does NOT weaken the control: the operative check is the sha256 of this VENDORED file, which is git-independent, and CI runs --strict WITHOUT --verify-provenance because git is not in the CI image. What it means is that --verify-provenance reads `unverified` here for a TERMINAL reason (unresolvable anywhere, forever) rather than the ordinary temporary one (git absent on this machine). Same word, two causes. Integrity is established; historicity is not. The anchor itself is deliberately git-FREE so its blindness is demonstrable in the CI image too - a git-dependent anchor reports UNKNOWN there and cannot be told from a crash, which is this issue's own defect class inside the tool built for it.

mutations.name: fixture-exclusion
mutations.protection: a deliberately-bad fixture under controls/*/cases/* is not this gate's population

mutations.name: sh-extension
mutations.protection: a .sh file is shell, whatever its first line says
mutations.why: STRUCTURALLY INEXPRESSIBLE while this anchor stands. Exercising the *.sh arm needs a BAD case whose offending file is a .sh file with no shebang - and the vendored anchor ed5349c globs *.sh, so it would CATCH that input and the control would be reported INERT ('the anchor is not blind') instead. The anchor's own blindness therefore forbids any committed BAD case on the whole .sh path. This is a real property of the pair, found by mutation and invisible to reading either file.

mutations.name: interpreter-allowlist
mutations.protection: an extensionless file is shell only when its shebang names a shell

mutations.name: env-shebang-resolution
mutations.protection: a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang resolves to bash, not to env

mutations.name: zero-matched-is-unknown
mutations.protection: 0 files examined is UNKNOWN, never 0 findings
mutations.why: STILL ACCEPTED, BUT FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN BEFORE - and the reason it used to give is now WRONG rather than merely incomplete, so it is corrected here instead of being left to read as current. It used to say this was inexpressible because the register carried no third expected verdict. #1129 added one: cases/unknown-zero-matched registers `expect: "UNKNOWN"`, is committed, and passes - the branch IS exercised end-to-end now, and it is the first refusal branch in this tree that any case reaches. WHAT MUTATION THEN REVEALED, which no amount of reading either file would have: this protection and `linter-crash-is-unknown` MUTUALLY MASK each other, so neither can be removed and noticed one at a time. MEASURED: with `-gt 0` weakened to `-ge 0` the gate does not report a false clean - it falls through and invokes shellcheck with ZERO file arguments, shellcheck exits 3 ('No files specified'), and the `*) unknown "shellcheck exited $RC"` arm reports UNKNOWN anyway. The case observes exactly what it registered and the battery stays green. The masking runs the other way too: weaken the crash arm instead and the zero-matched check fires first, so shellcheck is never reached. NO CASE INPUT CAN SEPARATE THEM. With COUNT=0 the linter is always invoked with no arguments and always exits 3, so the two protections are structurally redundant on the only path that reaches either - a property of the gate, not a gap in the register. What DOES distinguish them is the MESSAGE ('0 shell files matched ... 0 examined is not 0 findings' versus 'shellcheck exited 3'), and this register scores verdicts rather than message text, deliberately. THE CASE IS NOT DECORATION, and that was checked rather than assumed: break the `unknown()` helper itself so the refusal branch reports CLEAN, and the control reports BLIND - 'it reported CLEAN on an input it cannot examine'. It catches the failure the branch exists to prevent; what it cannot catch is the removal of one of two protections that produce the same verdict. What would move this: a probe that applies mutations in COMBINATION, which would reach both at once. Single-mutation probing cannot, by construction.

mutations.name: newline-path-audit
mutations.protection: a path this enumeration cannot carry safely is refused, not mangled
mutations.why: INPUT CANNOT BE COMMITTED - and this is now the ONLY thing blocking it, which is a change from what this entry used to say. The verdict vocabulary reached it: #1129 added `expect: "UNKNOWN"` and a case CAN now register this gate's refusal (see cases/unknown-zero-matched, which exercises the same `unknown` helper on the zero-matched branch). What remains is the input alone: this branch fires on a filename containing a NEWLINE, and git cannot carry such a path portably in a checked-out fixture, so no committed case tree can produce it. What would move this: an input mechanism that materialises a case tree at run time rather than checking it out - which is a change to the register, not to this gate, and is not proposed here.

mutations.name: option-terminator
mutations.protection: a file NAMED like a flag is an argument, not an option

mutations.name: unreadable-is-unknown
mutations.protection: a file that could not be read leaves the population unclassified
mutations.why: INPUT CANNOT BE COMMITTED - and, as above, this is now the only blocker; the verdict vocabulary reached it in #1129. The branch fires on a file the process cannot READ, and git records only the executable bit, so a checked-out fixture is always readable by the user who checked it out. A `chmod` at run time would work and is exactly what a committed case cannot do. What would move this: the same run-time case-materialisation the entry above names.

mutations.name: linter-absent-is-unknown
mutations.protection: no linter means nothing was examined, not nothing was found
mutations.why: A PROPERTY OF THE HOST, NOT OF ANY CASE TREE. The branch fires when shellcheck is off PATH, which no `--root` can arrange. Two register features come close and neither reaches it: #1117's UNAVAILABLE is an OBSERVATION the harness makes rather than a registrable expectation, and its cross-case contradiction check makes an unavailability report UNRESOLVED whenever another case through the same gate produced a real verdict - which every run on a host that HAS shellcheck does. #1129's UNKNOWN does not reach it either, and by construction: precedence consults `unavailable_signal` BEFORE `unknown_signal`, so this gate's tool-absent line is observed as UNAVAILABLE and never as a refusal a case could demand. That ordering is deliberate (it is what keeps a missing binary from being reported as a gate alarm), so this gap is a consequence of a protection rather than an oversight. What would move this: a per-case environment declaration in the register - naming it, not implementing it.

mutations.name: linter-crash-is-unknown
mutations.protection: a linter that failed to RUN is not a findings verdict
mutations.why: MASKED BY A SIBLING PROTECTION, plus no independent input reaches it - and the first half was found by mutation under #1129, not by reading. This arm fires when shellcheck exits something that is neither 0 nor 1. There IS a reachable route: with zero files to lint, shellcheck exits 3 ('No files specified'). But that route is unreachable on the UNMUTATED gate, because `zero-matched-is-unknown` refuses first and the linter is never invoked. The two protections mutually mask each other under single mutation - see that entry, which carries the measurement in full. NO OTHER INPUT REACHES IT EITHER, and this was MEASURED rather than argued (#1129, shellcheck 0.10.0): a binary-content .sh, a .sh with a `#!/usr/bin/perl` shebang, an empty .sh and a CRLF .sh each exited 1, reported as ordinary findings (SC2148, SC1071, SC1017). ShellCheck reserves 2+ for files it could not PROCESS and for bad invocation, neither of which a committed case tree arranges through this gate while at least one file is matched. THE VERDICT VOCABULARY IS NOT THE BLOCKER. Were such an input found, `expect: "UNKNOWN"` would register it today - that is what #1129 added, and cases/unknown-zero-matched is a working example of it. What would move this: an input shellcheck exits 2 on that this gate still classifies as shell, or a probe that mutates in combination.

mutations.name: root-must-be-a-directory
mutations.protection: a root that is not a directory is UNKNOWN, not clean
mutations.why: THE REGISTER'S OWN CASE PRECONDITION REFUSES IT, which is a different blocker from the two above and from the three below, and the distinction is the point (#1129 acceptance criterion 3). The input here is a `--root` that is NOT a directory; `check-negative-controls.evaluate()` requires `case_path.is_dir()` and reports `case input missing` otherwise, so such a case cannot be registered at all. The verdict vocabulary is not what stops this one - an UNKNOWN expectation would be honoured fine if the input could be handed over. What would move this: allowing a case `input` to name a FILE. That was considered under #1129 and deliberately not done - the precondition is load-bearing elsewhere, and relaxing a guard to test a neighbouring gate trades a real protection for a test.

mutations.name: git-enumeration-failure
mutations.protection: a file list that failed partway is incomplete, not short
mutations.why: A PROPERTY OF THE ENVIRONMENT, NOT OF THE TREE UNDER --root. The branch fires when `git ls-files` fails PARTWAY, yielding a short list and, without this check, a clean verdict over an incomplete population. No committed case tree can make git fail mid-enumeration. As with the two entries above, the verdict vocabulary is not what blocks it: #1129's UNKNOWN expectation would register the refusal if the condition could be produced. What would move this: a case that substitutes a failing `git` on PATH - which is the same per-case environment declaration `linter-absent-is-unknown` names, and would close both.
